subject: Post-call: head-to-head probe plan and immediate test asks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Evans <tom.evans@graystone.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@hypercloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: head-to-head probe plan and immediate test asks

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment on what matters for Graystone's latency-sensitive search product. Quick recap and next steps so we can lock the lab window next week.

Recap (short):
- Goal: validate p95/p99 latency and steady-state tokens/sec for your production prompt set across three providers: Redwood hosted API (redwood-open-v2-13B), HyperCloud managed inference, and Hyperscaler endpoint (your current baseline).
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (steady-state), cold-start tail, and error/retry rate.
- Sequence lengths: 64 (chat snippets), 256 (long prompts), 1024 (document summaries).

Immediate asks from Graystone:
1) Share a sample of production queries (anonymized) — you mentioned a ~2k snippet sample.
2) Provide API keys or short-term test credentials for Hyperscaler endpoint if you want us to run a blind head-to-head (preferred).
3) Confirm acceptable test window (we proposed Wed–Thu next week, 4h/day).

Proposed test matrix (attached: redwood-probe-specs-v1.pdf):
- Models: redwood-open-v2-13B (hosted), hypercloud-infer-13B, hyperscaler-13B
- Quantization variants: FP16 baseline, 8-bit quant where supported
- Sequence lengths: 64 / 256 / 1024
- Concurrency/clients: 1 (latency single-shot), 8 (typical concurrency), 32 (burst)
- Run cadence: ramp 5 mins -> steady 25 mins per cell -> cool down 5 mins
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency (client-observed), tokens/sec at server-side, CPU/GPU utilization (if partner shares), error rate, retry/backoff behavior

Timeline / next steps:
- Today: Graystone to drop sample queries + any sandbox keys (attachment preferred).
- Tue: Redwood prepares test harness and shares exact curl/test commands + Drive folder.
- Wed/Thu: Run lab window; Redwood shares raw logs + summary within 24h.
- Fri: 30-min readout + recommended optimizations (routing, caching, quantization).

Attachments: redwood-probe-specs-v1.pdf, mutual_action_plan_graystone.xlsx

If that looks good I’ll lock the Wed/Thu slots and share the Drive folder + runbook.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Post-call: head-to-head probe plan and immediate test asks

Thanks Vanessa — this is exactly the level of detail we need. I uploaded an anonymized set of ~2k queries (attached) and a short readme on traffic patterns. A few clarifications: 

1) For the Hyperscaler endpoint we can provision a time-limited key — I’ll send that to your secure inbox by EOD. If it’s easier to have you run everything from your infra, fine.
2) Our critical window is our 99th pct latency for 64-token queries; anything above ~350ms at p99 starts to degrade UX.
3) We don’t currently have GPU utilization exposed to external vendors; you can measure tokens/sec from responses and we'll provide server-side metrics after the run.

I attached: graystone-prod-queries.json and readme_prod_traffic.md (see Drive link in the attachment metadata). Wed morning works better for us if you can start then.

Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: head-to-head probe plan and immediate test asks

Thanks — couple of quick engineering notes and a refined test matrix from my side.

Engineering notes (internal focus):
- We will run the harness from two client locations (us-west and us-east) to capture region variance; keep Graystone’s Hyperscaler key limited to the us-west region if that’s where production is.
- For tokens/sec we’ll capture server-time per token when the provider exposes it; otherwise we’ll infer from response duration + token count.
- Include a simple prefix/KV cache sweep: run with cold cache and then with one-minute warmed prefix cache to show caching delta.

Refined test matrix (new columns):
- Warm vs cold cache (cold -> warm after 5 identical prompts)
- Retry/backoff stress: configure 1% injected failure to validate recovery latency
- Model variants: baseline 13B vs quantized 8-bit (if HyperCloud supports)

Operational asks for Graystone (small):
- Confirm whether you want us to include your A/B split logic in the client (we can do server-side routing but recommend client-side to match production split).
- Share any strict PII rules for the sample queries (anonymized copy is fine).

If you give the green light I’ll schedule the harness run, and Marissa can coordinate the readout slide deck.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

Perfect — thanks for the files and the note on the p99 threshold. Quick confirmation and next steps from our side: 

- We have the sample queries (graystone-prod-queries.json).
- Please send the Hyperscaler time-limited key to ops@redwood.ai (we will restrict it to run IPs only).
- We’ll spin up the harness and share the exact runbook + curl commands by EOD Tue (link included).
- Tentative run: Wed 08:00–12:00 PT — we’ll do two 90-min steady-state windows (64/256 sequences) and a final 60-min 1024 run.

Deliverables after the run: raw logs, p50/p95/p99 tables, tokens/sec graphs, and a short 6-slide readout with recommended changes (routing, batch sizes, quantization). Expect the readout Fri 10:00 PT.

If you want, we can also include an optional blind A/B where Graystone does not know which provider corresponds to which set (helps avoid bias). Let me know.

Thanks — locking Wed morning now.
